newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end off on Wall St, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end off on Wall St, profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean shares closed weaker for the second session in a row with the market undercut by Wall Street's slide and a wave of profit-taking, said traders.
Stocks are seen moving sideways at Friday's opening, although much depends on foreign investors who have driven the bolsa's rally this year, they said.
"The real wild card is what foreign investors will do," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano.
The 40-share index ended down 0.79 percent at 117.44 points. The general index lost 0.55 percent to 5,408.15 points in light turnover of 9.7 billion pesos.
Technical analyses show the bolsa should be moving in the 115-118 point range rather than the 120-point high hit earlier this week, said Eckel.
Profit-taking is likely to continue in coming sessions to bring the bourse firmly within these limits, traders said.
"Profit-taking will go on as prices have been way too high. People are having to pay a significant premium to get into this market," said one trader.
On Friday, investors will focus on companies' annual results which must be released by Monday, they said.
Corporate earnings published Friday, which included Enersis and Soquimich, were in line with expectations, they said.

Declining issues included telecom Telex, down 3.68 percent at 1,310 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, down 2.28 percent at 1,202 pesos and glass producer Cristales which shed 1.66 percent to 2,970 pesos.
Winners included supermarket chain Santa Isabel, up 1.27 percent at 800 pesos and drug-maker LabChile which rose 1.25 percent to 405 pesos.
